titleEn: While We Wait, Let Us Play!

pages.text: "Is Dad's boat still not here?" Lolo stomped in yellow boots to the end of the pier. Not one boat was visible. "I want to be first to catch the rope."
Lolo stamped impatiently. "When will he come—?" Riri sat fanning herself with her yellow hat. "I do not like waiting. I will just go!" Lolo said.
Lolo kicked at the pier post. Splash into a puddle! Their trousers got soaked. Still, the sea was empty.
Mom came to the pier with a basket. "Lolo, shall we play while we wait?" "Play?" Lolo stopped stomping.
"While we wait, let us play!" Mom pointed at the sky. "Can you count the seagulls?" Riri spread her fingers and began. "One, two, three..."
Lolo joined in. "Four, five, six—oh, one flew away!" Losing count, Lolo started at one again and laughed.
Now Lolo's turn. "That cloud looks like Dad's boat!" "Then that one is a huge fish!" Riri drew a line in the sky with her finger. A cloud boat chased a cloud fish.
"While we wait, let us play!" Lolo sang, looking at the clouds. Then, far away, putt, putt, putt—Dad's boat was coming!
The motorboat reached the pier. Lolo caught the rope Dad threw. "I was not bored at all! One, count seagulls! Two, change clouds into things! Three, take turns!" Riri nodded beside Lolo.
Mom kissed Lolo's cheek. "Waiting passes quickly when it becomes play." Lolo tapped the rope tied to the post. "While we wait, let us play!"
